name: Daniel’s accusers
charge: Seeking occasion against Daniel and finding none; procuring a decree by the law of the Medes and Persians that no man petition any god or man for thirty days save the king, to take him in the law of his God; assembling to find him praying and pressing the king to cast him to the lions
summary: The presidents and princes under Darius sought occasion against Daniel and found no fault in him except concerning the law of his God, so they had the king sign an unchangeable decree that no one petition any god or man but the king for thirty days (Daniel 6:4-9). They found Daniel praying toward Jerusalem as before, reported him, and pressed the king until Daniel was cast to the lions (Daniel 6:10-17). God shut the lions’ mouths, and the king had the accusers, their children, and their wives cast into the den, where the lions broke their bones before they reached the bottom (Daniel 6:22-24).
offenseFull: Darius set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom and three presidents over them, Daniel first, and thought to set him over the whole realm because an excellent spirit was in him (Daniel 6:1-3). The presidents and princes sought occasion against him concerning the kingdom and found none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was in him (Daniel 6:4). The class renders their thinking: we cannot find fault with his work, so we will use his religion against him. The study note says they really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God (Daniel 6:5).

They came to the king claiming that all the rulers had agreed, and persuaded him to sign a decree that anyone who asked a petition of any god or man but the king for thirty days be cast into the den of lions, by the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not change (Daniel 6:6-9). The teaching explains that in the Persian empire a decree once sent out could not be reversed, and the king’s counsellors held him to it. They gathered, found Daniel praying and making supplication to his God, reminded the king of his decree, and reported that Daniel, of the captivity of Judah, did not regard him or his decree (Daniel 6:10-13). The king laboured till sundown to deliver him, but they pressed him that no decree of the Medes and Persians could be changed (Daniel 6:14-15). The class reads beside this the account in Bel and the Dragon, where the people of Babylon said the king had become a Jew and threatened to destroy him and his house unless he delivered Daniel to them (Bel and the Dragon 1:28-30). The king, displeased with himself, commanded Daniel cast in, saying that the God he served continually would deliver him, and the den was sealed (Daniel 6:16-17).
judgmentFull: The king passed the night fasting, with no music and no sleep, and hurried to the den at dawn; Daniel answered that God had sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths, because he was found innocent before God and had done the king no hurt (Daniel 6:18-22). The class sets beside it the Bel and the Dragon account, in which seven lions were kept hungry so they would devour Daniel, the prophet Habakkuk was carried by an angel to feed him in the den, and the king cried that the God of Daniel is great and there is none other (Bel and the Dragon 1:31-41).

Then the king commanded that the men who had accused Daniel be cast into the den, they, their children, and their wives, and the lions overpowered them and broke all their bones before they came to the bottom (Daniel 6:24). The class says the lions that had been held back from Daniel devoured those who set him up. The law of the false witness is to do to him as he thought to do to his brother (Deuteronomy 19:16-19), and the study note on that law says that whoever falsely accuses a man of a crime worthy of death is put to death, because that is what he intended for his neighbour, and that false witnesses arising among our own people were part of why the nation fell into captivity. When a man’s ways please the Lord, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him (Proverbs 16:7). Darius then wrote to every people that in all his dominion men should tremble before the God of Daniel, the living God whose kingdom shall not be destroyed (Daniel 6:25-27).

lawsResolved.text: Do not join your hand with a wicked man to be an unrighteous witness.
If a witness is found to be a false witness by testifying falsely against his brother, then he shall receive the punishment that the accused brethren would have received if guilty.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
Deceit and fraud a characteristic of the wicked.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).

Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.

Then they came near, and spake before the king concerning the king’s decree; Hast thou not signed a decree, that every man that shall ask a petition of any God or man within thirty days, save of thee, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered and said, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.

Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed.
Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel, and cast him into the den of lions. Now the king spake and said unto Daniel, Thy God whom thou servest continually, he will deliver thee.
And a stone was brought, and laid upon the mouth of the den; and the king sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his lords; that the purpose might not be changed concerning Daniel.
My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.

Then was the king exceeding glad for him, and commanded that they should take Daniel up out of the den. So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his God.

When they of Babylon heard that, they took great indignation, and conspired against the king, saying, The king is become a Jew, and he hath destroyed Bel, he hath slain the dragon, and put the priests to death.
So they came to the king, and said, Deliver us Daniel, or else we will destroy thee and thine house.
Now when the king saw that they pressed him sore, being constrained, he delivered Daniel unto them:

Then the king arose very early in the morning, and went in haste unto the den of lions.

My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
Who cast him into the lions’ den: where he was six days.
And in the den there were seven lions, and they had given them every day two carcases, and two sheep: which then were not given to them, to the intent they might devour Daniel.
Now there was in Jewry a prophet, called Habbacuc, who had made pottage, and had broken bread in a bowl, and was going into the field, for to bring it to the reapers.
But the angel of the Lord said unto Habbacuc, Go, carry the dinner that thou hast into Babylon unto Daniel, who is in the lions’ den.
And Habbacuc said, Lord, I never saw Babylon; neither do I know where the den is.
Then the angel of the Lord took him by the crown, and bare him by the hair of his head, and through the vehemency of his spirit set him in Babylon over the den.
And Habbacuc cried, saying, O Daniel, Daniel, take the dinner which God hath sent thee.
And Daniel said, Thou hast remembered me, O God: neither hast thou forsaken them that seek thee and love thee.
So Daniel arose, and did eat: and the angel of the Lord set Habbacuc in his own place again immediately.
Upon the seventh day the king went to bewail Daniel: and when he came to the den, he looked in, and behold, Daniel was sitting.
Then cried the king with a loud voice, saying, Great art Lord God of Daniel, and there is none other beside thee.

And the king commanded, and they brought those men which had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions, them, their children, and their wives; and the lions had the mastery of them, and brake all their bones in pieces or ever they came at the bottom of the den.
If a false witness rise up against any man to testify against him that which is wrong;
Then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges, which shall be in those days;
And the judges shall make diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness be a false witness, and hath testified falsely against his brother;
Then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother: so shalt thou put the evil away from among you.
